Players 'definitely' believe in Parker, says Bowen
- Published
West Ham captain Jarrod Bowen says the players "definitely" believe new manager Scott Parker can turn around their season.
Tuesday's 1-0 defeat at Portsmouth leaves the Hammers 13th in the Championship following last season's relegation from the Premier League.
Former West Ham captain Parker replaced the sacked Nuno Espirito Santo at the beginning of November but has failed to win any of his four matches in charge.
Bowen, speaking at an EFL Power of 72 campaign event, told BBC Radio London: "You don't want to be drawn into saying 'we're unlucky', but the chances that we've had, we've been very unfortunate to lose.
"But ultimately we know what football is - it's a results business. He's a very, very positive manager. He's very demanding, passionate, he's played for the club.
"He understands what it means to play for West Ham, so we all have a really good understanding even in the small time we've been working together."
Asked if the players feel Parker can reverse the Hammers' fortunes and lead them up the table, Bowen said: "Yes definitely."
The forward, 29, joined West Ham from Hull City, then in the Championship, in 2020 and chose to stay at the club this summer despite their relegation.
Tuesday's loss at Fratton Park was his 300th appearance for the Londoners and he insists he does not feel the burden of expectation to bounce straight back to the top flight.
"I probably thrive on it because you don't let something that's positive wear you down," he adds.
"When I first came here there were probably question marks about me because I was signing from the Championship to a Premier League side.
"Then its all about having your opportunity and then it's down to you to go out and show everyone what you can do."

Parker made more than 500 appearances for club and country in his 20-year playing career and as a manager has led Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley to promotion from the Championship.
The 46-year-old is determined to support his players as much as possible.
"I never experienced what these professional athletes experience now, in terms of being in the spotlight. The general noise around players and clubs is tenfold, really. So, I'm very consistent in what I demand and ask for."
Parker added he tries to "be rational, in terms of not getting on the rollercoaster, the hype or the ridicule" that the game sometimes provides.
"We know we're a big side in this division and we have to understand that, live with that and deal with that in order to get through that and get the right results," he said.
